From 76f9377cd2ab7a9220c25d33940d9ca20d368172 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 17:51:45 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] writeback: don't block sync for filesystems with no data
 integrity guarantees

Add a SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY superblock flag for filesystems that cannot
guarantee data persistence on sync (eg fuse). For superblocks with this
flag set, sync kicks off writeback of dirty inodes but does not wait
for the flusher threads to complete the writeback.

This replaces the per-inode AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY mapping flag added in
commit f9a49aa302a0 ("fs/writeback: skip AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY mappings
in wait_sb_inodes()"). The flag belongs at the superblock level because
data integrity is a filesystem-wide property, not a per-inode one.
Having this flag at the superblock level also allows us to skip having
to iterate every dirty inode in wait_sb_inodes() only to skip each inode
individually.

Prior to this commit, mappings with no data integrity guarantees skipped
waiting on writeback completion but still waited on the flusher threads
to finish initiating the writeback. Waiting on the flusher threads is
unnecessary. This commit kicks off writeback but does not wait on the
flusher threads. This change properly addresses a recent report [1] for
a suspend-to-RAM hang seen on fuse-overlayfs that was caused by waiting
on the flusher threads to finish:

Workqueue: pm_fs_sync pm_fs_sync_work_fn
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 __schedule+0x457/0x1720
 schedule+0x27/0xd0
 wb_wait_for_completion+0x97/0xe0
 sync_inodes_sb+0xf8/0x2e0
 __iterate_supers+0xdc/0x160
 ksys_sync+0x43/0xb0
 pm_fs_sync_work_fn+0x17/0xa0
 process_one_work+0x193/0x350
 worker_thread+0x1a1/0x310
 kthread+0xfc/0x240
 ret_from_fork+0x243/0x280
 ret_from_fork_asm+0x1a/0x30
 </TASK>

On fuse this is problematic because there are paths that may cause the
flusher thread to block (eg if systemd freezes the user session cgroups
first, which freezes the fuse daemon, before invoking the kernel
suspend. The kernel suspend triggers ->write_node() which on fuse issues
a synchronous setattr request, which cannot be processed since the
daemon is frozen. Or if the daemon is buggy and cannot properly complete
writeback, initiating writeback on a dirty folio already under writeback
leads to writeback_get_folio() -> folio_prepare_writeback() ->
unconditional wait on writeback to finish, which will cause a hang).
This commit restores fuse to its prior behavior before tmp folios were
removed, where sync was essentially a no-op.

[1] https://lore.kernel.org/linux-fsdevel/CAJnrk1a-asuvfrbKXbEwwDSctvemF+6zfhdnuzO65Pt8HsFSRw@mail.gmail.com/T/#m632c4648e9cafc4239299887109ebd880ac6c5c1

Fixes: 0c58a97f919c ("fuse: remove tmp folio for writebacks and internal rb tree")
Reported-by: John <therealgraysky@proton.me>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260320005145.2483161-2-joannelkoong@gmail.com
Reviewed-by: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>
Reviewed-by: David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Christian Brauner <brauner@kernel.org>

diff --git a/include/linux/fs/super_types.h b/include/linux/fs/super_types.h
index fa7638b81246..383050e7fdf5 100644
--- a/include/linux/fs/super_types.h
+++ b/include/linux/fs/super_types.h
@@ -338,5 +338,6 @@ struct super_block {
 #define SB_I_NOUMASK	0x00001000	/* VFS does not apply umask */
 #define SB_I_NOIDMAP	0x00002000	/* No idmapped mounts on this superblock */
 #define SB_I_ALLOW_HSM	0x00004000	/* Allow HSM events on this superblock */
+#define SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY	0x00008000 /* fs cannot guarantee data persistence on sync */
 
 #endif /* _LINUX_FS_SUPER_TYPES_H */

diff --git a/fs/fs-writeback.c b/fs/fs-writeback.c
index d8dac1931595..3c75ee025bda 100644
--- a/fs/fs-writeback.c
+++ b/fs/fs-writeback.c
@@ -2787,13 +2787,8 @@ static void wait_sb_inodes(struct super_block *sb)
 		 * The mapping can appear untagged while still on-list since we
 		 * do not have the mapping lock. Skip it here, wb completion
 		 * will remove it.
-		 *
-		 * If the mapping does not have data integrity semantics,
-		 * there's no need to wait for the writeout to complete, as the
-		 * mapping cannot guarantee that data is persistently stored.
 		 */
-		if (!mapping_tagged(mapping, PAGECACHE_TAG_WRITEBACK) ||
-		    mapping_no_data_integrity(mapping))
+		if (!mapping_tagged(mapping, PAGECACHE_TAG_WRITEBACK))
 			continue;
 
 		spin_unlock_irq(&sb->s_inode_wblist_lock);
@@ -2928,6 +2923,17 @@ void sync_inodes_sb(struct super_block *sb)
 	 */
 	if (bdi == &noop_backing_dev_info)
 		return;
+
+	/*
+	 * If the superblock has SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY set, there's no need to
+	 * wait for the writeout to complete, as the filesystem cannot guarantee
+	 * data persistence on sync. Just kick off writeback and return.
+	 */
+	if (sb->s_iflags & SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY) {
+		wakeup_flusher_threads_bdi(bdi, WB_REASON_SYNC);
+		return;
+	}
+
 	WARN_ON(!rwsem_is_locked(&sb->s_umount));
 
 	/* protect against inode wb switch, see inode_switch_wbs_work_fn() */

diff --git a/fs/fuse/inode.c b/fs/fuse/inode.c
index e57b8af06be9..c795abe47a4f 100644
--- a/fs/fuse/inode.c
+++ b/fs/fuse/inode.c
@@ -1709,6 +1709,7 @@ static void fuse_sb_defaults(struct super_block *sb)
 	sb->s_export_op = &fuse_export_operations;
 	sb->s_iflags |= SB_I_IMA_UNVERIFIABLE_SIGNATURE;
 	sb->s_iflags |= SB_I_NOIDMAP;
+	sb->s_iflags |= SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY;
 	if (sb->s_user_ns != &init_user_ns)
 		sb->s_iflags |= SB_I_UNTRUSTED_MOUNTER;
 	sb->s_flags &= ~(SB_NOSEC | SB_I_VERSION);

diff --git a/include/linux/pagemap.h b/include/linux/pagemap.h
index ec442af3f886..31a848485ad9 100644
--- a/include/linux/pagemap.h
+++ b/include/linux/pagemap.h
@@ -210,7 +210,6 @@ enum mapping_flags {
 	AS_WRITEBACK_MAY_DEADLOCK_ON_RECLAIM = 9,
 	AS_KERNEL_FILE = 10,	/* mapping for a fake kernel file that shouldn't
 				   account usage to user cgroups */
-	AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY = 11, /* no data integrity guarantees */
 	/* Bits 16-25 are used for FOLIO_ORDER */
 	AS_FOLIO_ORDER_BITS = 5,
 	AS_FOLIO_ORDER_MIN = 16,
@@ -346,16 +345,6 @@ static inline bool mapping_writeback_may_deadlock_on_reclaim(const struct addres
 	return test_bit(AS_WRITEBACK_MAY_DEADLOCK_ON_RECLAIM, &mapping->flags);
 }
 
-static inline void mapping_set_no_data_integrity(struct address_space *mapping)
-{
-	set_bit(AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY, &mapping->flags);
-}
-
-static inline bool mapping_no_data_integrity(const struct address_space *mapping)
-{
-	return test_bit(AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY, &mapping->flags);
-}
-
 static inline gfp_t mapping_gfp_mask(const struct address_space *mapping)
 {
 	return mapping->gfp_mask;
--

diff --git a/fs/fuse/file.c b/fs/fuse/file.c
index b1bb7153cb78..676fd9856bfb 100644
--- a/fs/fuse/file.c
+++ b/fs/fuse/file.c
@@ -3201,10 +3201,8 @@ void fuse_init_file_inode(struct inode *inode, unsigned int flags)
 
 	inode->i_fop = &fuse_file_operations;
 	inode->i_data.a_ops = &fuse_file_aops;
-	if (fc->writeback_cache) {
+	if (fc->writeback_cache)
 		mapping_set_writeback_may_deadlock_on_reclaim(&inode->i_data);
-		mapping_set_no_data_integrity(&inode->i_data);
-	}
 
 	INIT_LIST_HEAD(&fi->write_files);
 	INIT_LIST_HEAD(&fi->queued_writes);

## Summary of the Patch

This patch introduces a new superblock-level flag `SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` to indicate filesystems that cannot guarantee data persistence on `sync()` (e.g., FUSE). This replaces the previous per-inode mapping flag `AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` which was introduced in an earlier commit.

### Modifications per File

1. **`include/linux/fs/super_types.h`**  
   - Added the new flag `SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` (value `0x00008000`) to the `s_iflags` bitmask.

2. **`fs/fs-writeback.c`**  
   - **`wait_sb_inodes()`**: Removed the check for `mapping_no_data_integrity()` that previously skipped waiting on writeback for mappings lacking data integrity guarantees.  
   - **`sync_inodes_sb()`**: Added an early return when `SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` is set on the superblock. Instead of waiting for flusher threads to complete, it only wakes the flusher threads (`wakeup_flusher_threads_bdi()`) and returns immediately.

3. **`fs/fuse/inode.c`**  
   - In `fuse_sb_defaults()`, added the flag `SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` to the superblock's `s_iflags`. This marks the entire FUSE filesystem as having no data integrity guarantees.

4. **`include/linux/pagemap.h`**  
   - Removed the `AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` enum bit and the associated helper functions `mapping_set_no_data_integrity()` and `mapping_no_data_integrity()`. These are no longer needed.

5. **`fs/fuse/file.c`**  
   - In `fuse_init_file_inode()`, removed the call to `mapping_set_no_data_integrity()`. The writeback cache flag remains but now only sets the deadlock-on-reclaim flag.

### Relationships Between Changes

The changes are tightly coupled:

- The **superblock flag** (`SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY`) is the core replacement for the **per-inode mapping flag** (`AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY`). Data integrity is a filesystem-wide property, so moving it to the superblock reduces overhead and simplifies code.

- In `fs/fs-writeback.c`, the removal of the per-mapping skip in `wait_sb_inodes()` and the addition of the early return in `sync_inodes_sb()` together achieve the intended behavior: for filesystems with `SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY`, writeback is initiated but neither per-inode writeback completion nor flusher thread completion is waited upon.

- In **FUSE** (`fs/fuse/inode.c` and `fs/fuse/file.c`), the flag is set at the superblock level, and the per-inode setting is removed. This ensures that all FUSE inodes (not just those with writeback cache) benefit from the new behavior. The change also avoids iterating all dirty inodes only to skip them individually.

- The removal of `AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` and its helpers from `include/linux/pagemap.h` cleans up the now-unused infrastructure.

### Overall Effect

The patch fixes a suspend-to-RAM hang on FUSE-overlayfs by preventing `sync()` from blocking on flusher threads that may never complete (e.g., if the FUSE daemon is frozen). It also simplifies code by moving the data integrity property from per-inode to per-superblock, reducing overhead in `wait_sb_inodes()`.

   - Removed the call to `mapping_set_no_data_integrity(&inode->i_data)` from `fuse_init_file_inode()`. The flag is no longer set per inode.

- The change in `sync_inodes_sb()` is the key behavioral fix: for FUSE (and any other filesystem with `SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY`), `sync` no longer waits for flusher threads (which could block indefinitely if the FUSE daemon is frozen or buggy). It merely initiates writeback and returns, restoring the pre‑tmp-folios behavior.
- The changes in `wait_sb_inodes()` are a simplification: since the integrity check is now done earlier in `sync_inodes_sb()`, there’s no need to skip individual inodes inside the waiter loop.

Having this flag at the superblock level also allows us to skip having
to iterate every dirty inode in wait_sb_inodes() only to skip each inode
individually.

Prior to this commit, mappings with no data integrity guarantees skipped
waiting on writeback completion but still waited on the flusher threads
to finish initiating the writeback. Waiting on the flusher threads is
unnecessary. This commit kicks off writeback but does not wait on the
flusher threads. This change properly addresses a recent report [1] for
a suspend-to-RAM hang seen on fuse-overlayfs that was caused by waiting
on the flusher threads to finish:

Workqueue: pm_fs_sync pm_fs_sync_work_fn
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 __schedule+0x457/0x1720
 schedule+0x27/0xd0
 wb_wait_for_completion+0x97/0xe0
 sync_inodes_sb+0xf8/0x2e0
 __iterate_supers+0xdc/0x160
 ksys_sync+0x43/0xb0
 pm_fs_sync_work_fn+0x17/0xa0
 process_one_work+0x193/0x350
 worker_thread+0x1a1/0x310
 kthread+0xfc/0x240
 ret_from_fork+0x243/0x280
 ret_from_fork_asm+0x1a/0x30
 </TASK>

On fuse this is problematic because there are paths that may cause the
flusher thread to block (eg if systemd freezes the user session cgroups
first, which freezes the fuse daemon, before invoking the kernel
suspend. The kernel suspend triggers ->write_node() which on fuse issues
a synchronous setattr request, which cannot be processed since the
daemon is frozen. Or if the daemon is buggy and cannot properly complete
writeback, initiating writeback on a dirty folio already under writeback
leads to writeback_get_folio() -> folio_prepare_writeback() ->
unconditional wait on writeback to finish, which will cause a hang).
This commit restores fuse to its prior behavior before tmp folios were
removed, where sync was essentially a no-op.

The patch replaces the per‑inode `AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` flag with a per‑superblock `SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` flag, representing that a filesystem (e.g. fuse) cannot guarantee data persistence on sync.

### Modifications in each file

1. **`include/linux/fs/super_types.h`**  
   Adds the new superblock flag `SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` (bit 0x00008000).

2. **`include/linux/pagemap.h`**  
   Removes the `AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` address_space flag and its helper functions (`mapping_set_no_data_integrity`, `mapping_no_data_integrity`).

3. **`fs/fuse/file.c`**  
   Removes the call to `mapping_set_no_data_integrity()` for fuse inodes using the writeback cache. The flag is now set at the superblock level.

4. **`fs/fuse/inode.c`**  
   In `fuse_sb_defaults()`, sets `SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` on all fuse superblocks.

5. **`fs/fs-writeback.c`**  
   - In `wait_sb_inodes()`: removes the check for `mapping_no_data_integrity()`.  
   - In `sync_inodes_sb()`: **before** the existing wait logic, checks for `SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY`. If set, it only kicks off writeback via `wakeup_flusher_threads_bdi()` and returns immediately, without waiting for flusher threads to complete.

### Relationships

The change centralizes the data‑integrity property from individual mappings (inodes) to the entire filesystem (superblock). This eliminates per‑inode iteration overhead in `wait_sb_inodes()` and, crucially, allows `sync_inodes_sb()` to avoid blocking when the filesystem cannot guarantee persistence. For fuse, this restores the pre‑tmp‑folio behavior where sync was effectively a no‑op, preventing hangs (e.g., during suspend‑to‑RAM when the fuse daemon is frozen).

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
wb_wait_for_completion(&done);  // in sync_inodes_sb()
```
Reason:
`sync_inodes_sb()` unconditionally waits for flusher threads to complete writeback via `wb_wait_for_completion()`, even for filesystems like fuse that cannot guarantee data persistence. When the fuse daemon is frozen or blocked (e.g., during suspend), the flusher thread may hang on synchronous requests, causing a system-wide stall.

The previous per-inode `mapping_no_data_integrity()` check in `wait_sb_inodes()` only skipped waiting on page writeback completion, but did not prevent this wait on the flusher threads.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
if (sb->s_iflags & SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY) {
    wakeup_flusher_threads_bdi(bdi, WB_REASON_SYNC);
    return;
}
// in sync_inodes_sb()
```
Reason:
This early exit at the start of `sync_inodes_sb()` checks the superblock flag `SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY`. For such filesystems (e.g., fuse), it simply kicks off writeback via `wakeup_flusher_threads_bdi()` and returns immediately, without waiting for the flusher threads or for page writeback to complete. This prevents the hang entirely. The corresponding per-inode check in `wait_sb_inodes()` is also removed as it is no longer needed.
